facts.statement: Current scientific consensus classifies Anoplosaurus as an armored dinosaur within the Ankylosauria, despite past classifications with ornithopods.
facts.quote: It has in the past been classified with either the armored dinosaurs or the ornithopods, but current thought has been in agreement with the "armored dinosaur" interpretation, placing it in the Ankylosauria.

facts.statement: Harry Govier Seeley named the genus Anoplosaurus in 1879 based on a partial skeleton uncovered at Reach, Cambridgeshire.
facts.quote: Harry Govier Seeley named this genus in 1879 for a disarticulated partial postcranial skeleton that had been uncovered no later than 1878 at Reach, Cambridgeshire

facts.statement: The generic name Anoplosaurus means "unarmed" because no armor plates were found in the original specimen.
facts.quote: The generic name, derived from the Greek hoplo~, a word element used in combinations, with the meaning of "armed", refers to the fact no armour plates had been discovered.

facts.statement: Seeley named a second species, Anoplosaurus major, in 1879 using vertebrae removed from material previously assigned to Acanthopholis stereocercus.
facts.quote: A second species, Anoplosaurus major, "the larger one", was named by Seeley in 1879 for a neck vertebra and three partial caudal vertebrae he removed from the material previously referred to Acanthopholis stereocercus

facts.statement: It is now believed that Anoplosaurus major is a chimeric species composed of a neck vertebra from an ankylosaur and tail vertebrae from an indeterminate iguanodont.
facts.quote: This species now appears to be chimeric, the neck vertebra coming from an ankylosaur, the caudals from an indeterminate iguanodont.

facts.statement: Pereda-Suberbiola and Barrett (1998) suggested the lack of armor in Anoplosaurus curtonotus was due to the animal's young age at death.
facts.quote: In 1998, Xabier Pereda-Suberbiola and Paul Barrett reexamined the material of Anoplosaurus curtonotus. They wrote that it all belonged to a "primitive" or basal member of the Nodosauridae, the lack of armor possibly due to the young age of the animal at death.

facts.statement: Anoplosaurus lived during the Middle Cretaceous, approximately 110 to 95 million years ago, in what is now Europe.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 110 y 95 millones de años, en el Albiense y Cenomaniense, en lo que es hoy Europa.

facts.statement: Anoplosaurus was likely a quadrupedal, low-slung herbivore with body armor for protection.
facts.quote: El anoplosaurio habría sido un cuadrúpedo, cuerpo bajo y compacto, herbívoro, con una armadura en su cuerpo para su protección.

facts.statement: Anoplosaurus reached a length of about 5.00 meters, a height of 1.70 meters, and an estimated weight of 2500 kilograms.
facts.quote: Llegó a medir alrededor de los 5,00 metros de largo, 1,70 de alto y con un peso estimado de 2500 kilogramos.

facts.statement: Seeley named the genus in 1879 based on a partial postcranial skeleton including jaw fragments, numerous vertebrae, pectoral girdle parts, limb bones, ribs, and other fragments found in the Cambridge Greensand Formation.
facts.quote: Harry Govier Seeley nombró este género en 1879 para un esqueleto postcranial parcial, integrado por fragmentos del dentario, numerosas vértebras del cuello, lomo, y sacro, las partes de la faja pectoral, fragmentos del húmero, piezas del fémur izquierdo, tibia izquierda, los huesos del pie, costillas, y otros fragmentos encontrados en Cambridge Formación Arena Verde de Cambridgeshire, Inglaterra.

facts.statement: The second species A. major is considered a chimera because its neck vertebra comes from an ankylosaur and its tail vertebrae from an indeterminate iguanodont.
facts.quote: Una segunda especie, A. major, fue nombrada por Seeley en 1879 para una vértebra del cuello y tres vértebras caudales parciales que él recogió de Acanthopholis stereocercus, de la misma formación que la especie tipo. Esta especie se considera como una quimera, ya que la vértebra del cuello proviene de un anquilosauriano, y las caudales de un iguanodóntido indeterminado.

facts.statement: Pereda-Suberbiola and Barrett (1998) proposed that Anoplosaurus curtonotus belonged to a primitive member of the Nodosauridae family and its lack of armor was likely due to its short age at death.
facts.quote: En 1998, Xabier Pereda-Suberbiola y Paul Barrett volvieron a examinar el material de Anoplosaurus curtonotus. Ellos escribieron que todo pertenecía a un miembro "primitivo" o basal de la familia Nodosauridae, la falta de armadura posiblemente se debía a la corta edad del animal a la muerte.

facts.statement: Anoplosaurus is classified within the superfamily Ankylosauria.
facts.quote: superfamilia: Ankylosauria

facts.statement: Anoplosaurus belongs to the family Nodosauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Nodosauridae

facts.statement: Anoplosaurus is placed in the subfamily Struthiosaurinae.
facts.quote: subfamilia: Struthiosaurinae

facts.statement: Pereda-Suberbiola and Barrett selected specimen SMC B55731, a right scapula, as the lectotype.
facts.quote: Pereda-Superbiola y Barrett seleccionaron al espécimen SMC B55731, una escápula derecha, como el lectotipo.

facts.statement: Pereda-Suberbiola and Barrett suggested the fossils might have been found in the Upper Gault Clay rather than the Cambridge Greensand because the skeletal elements appeared to belong to a single individual.
facts.quote: Pereda-Superbiola y Barrett consideraron que era posible que el descubrimiento, de hecho, no se haya hecho en la arena verde de Cambridge, sino en la arcilla Gault también del Albianense superior, debido a que los elementos esqueléticos parecían haber pertenecido a un solo individuo que podría contradecir que una procedencia de los depósitos marinos de arena verde.

facts.statement: Researchers Suberbiola and Barrett identified Anoplosaurus as a diagnostic taxon closely related to Silvisaurus condrayi and Texasetes pleurohalio.
facts.quote: El volumen de fósiles cretáceo de los vertebrados de 1999 contiene un artículo sobre los nodosáuridos ingleses en los cuales Suberbiola y Barrett encuentran que Anoplosaurus es una taxón diagnóstico relacionado cercanamente con Silvisaurus condrayi y Texasetes pleurohalio.

facts.statement: While historically classified with either armored dinosaurs or ornithopods, current consensus places Anoplosaurus in Ankylosauria.
facts.quote: En el pasado se ha clasificado, ya sea con los dinosaurios acorazados o con los ornitópodos, pero el pensamiento actual está de acuerdo con la interpretación de "dinosaurio acorazado", colocándolo en Ankylosauria.

facts.statement: Anoplosaurus is classified within the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: The genus Anoplosaurus was named by Seeley in 1879.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Anoplosaurus (genus), Seeley 1879

facts.statement: Anoplosaurus lived during the Cenomanian stage, between 100.5 and 93.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Cenomanian (100.5 to 93.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: There is only one recorded fossil occurrence of Anoplosaurus in the Paleobiology Database.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 1
